industry_workflow.overview: How an Applied AI Solutions Engineer executes client and enterprise deliverables in production:

stages.name: Business Discovery & Scoping
stages.desc: Identify high-friction business workflows, stakeholder requirements, data boundaries, and clear success criteria.

stages.name: Feasibility & Architecture Planning
stages.desc: Evaluate AI feasibility, latency thresholds, error tolerances, model economics, and architectural boundaries.

stages.name: System Architecture Design
stages.desc: Blueprint data flows, vector stores, API contracts, state graphs, external integrations, and human approval gates.

stages.name: Data Ingestion & Knowledge Engineering
stages.desc: Extract, normalize, and chunk corporate documentation; generate embeddings and index inside pgvector with metadata.

stages.name: Model & Tool Protocol Selection
stages.desc: Select optimal frontier and open-weight models balancing reasoning quality, token economics, context window, and latency.

stages.name: API & Tool Integration
stages.desc: Connect external software via REST endpoints, webhooks, CRMs, and standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

stages.name: Agent & Workflow Construction
stages.desc: Build deterministic agent state machines in LangGraph, tool-calling loops, and event-driven automation nodes in n8n.

stages.name: Quantitative Evaluation & Testing
stages.desc: Benchmark against golden datasets; measure retrieval accuracy, tool selection correctness, latency, and faithfulness.

stages.name: Defensive Security & Privacy Hardening
stages.desc: Enforce prompt injection mitigation, role-based tool authorization, PII redaction, and strict API secret protection.

stages.name: Containerization & Cloud Deployment
stages.desc: Package microservices using multi-stage Dockerfiles, configure FastAPI endpoints, and deploy to scalable cloud platforms.

stages.name: Distributed Observability & Monitoring
stages.desc: Track production latency, token costs, drift, error rates, and user feedback traces using Langfuse or LangSmith.

stages.name: Handover, Documentation & ROI Review
stages.desc: Deliver comprehensive repository documentation, train client operators, present measurable ROI impact, and establish maintenance retainers.

faq.question: Who is this course suitable for?
faq.answer: This flagship 9-month program is built for aspiring AI solutions engineers, software and IT learners seeking production-grade agentic skills, automation specialists upgrading from no-code workflows to software engineering, technical career switchers entering applied AI, and technical consultants or entrepreneurs building scalable AI systems for enterprise clients.

faq.question: Do I need a prior computer science degree or advanced programming background to enroll?
faq.answer: No computer science degree or prior programming experience is required. Basic computer literacy, logical reasoning, and comfort navigating standard software are sufficient to start. The curriculum begins with dedicated foundational modules (Python, APIs, and SQL) in Months 1 and 2 that establish developer-grade competencies from scratch before introducing advanced agentic and RAG architectures.

faq.question: How deep does the Python curriculum go, and is it sufficient for production AI engineering?
faq.answer: The Python curriculum spans 40 guided hours in Module 02 plus continuous application throughout all subsequent modules. It covers professional-grade Python 3.12+, including object-oriented programming, type hints, modern data validation with Pydantic v2, asynchronous programming with AsyncIO, package management with uv/pip, automated unit testing with Pytest, and defensive error handling. You learn the exact software engineering standards required to build, test, and maintain production AI backends.

faq.question: What backend technologies and API architectures will I build with?
faq.answer: You master backend engineering using FastAPI (Python's leading modern asynchronous web framework). You build production REST services featuring OpenAPI documentation, Pydantic request/response validation, API key and Bearer token authentication, Server-Sent Events (SSE) for streaming model tokens, rate limiting, and structured logging. These backend services form the production interface for your RAG knowledge engines and autonomous agents.

faq.question: How is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and vector data engineering taught?
faq.answer: RAG is covered extensively in Module 08 (32 guided hours) and applied in multiple portfolio builds. You learn production document parsing, semantic chunking strategies, dense embedding generation, and high-performance vector indexing with pgvector inside PostgreSQL. You build hybrid search pipelines combining BM25 keyword matching with vector cosine similarity, implement cross-encoder reranking (Cohere Rerank), and enforce strict citation grounding to prevent model hallucinations.

faq.question: What will I learn about the OpenAI Agents SDK and tool-enabled agents?
faq.answer: You learn to build tool-enabled agents using the modern OpenAI Agents SDK and OpenAI Responses API. The training covers defining executable tools using JSON schemas, handling multi-turn tool calling, managing conversation state, implementing agent handoffs between specialized roles, applying guardrails, and tracing execution runs. (Note: The discontinued OpenAI Assistants API v1/v2 is not taught, focusing instead on forward-looking modern SDKs).

faq.question: How are multi-agent architectures and LangGraph state machines implemented?
faq.answer: Module 09 (36 guided hours) is dedicated to advanced agent architectures using LangGraph. You learn state graph modeling, cyclic node execution, conditional edges, shared state schemas, persistence and checkpointing with PostgreSQL, and human-in-the-loop interruption patterns. You build multi-agent teams where specialized planner, researcher, data analyst, and reviewer agents collaborate deterministically to solve complex multi-step enterprise workflows.

faq.question: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and how is it covered in the course?
faq.answer: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the open standard that connects AI models securely to local and enterprise systems. Module 10 (24 guided hours) covers the official specification. You build both custom MCP servers (using Python FastMCP SDK) and MCP clients. You implement stdio transport for local tool integration and Streamable HTTP for network services, exposing enterprise databases, file systems, and business APIs with secure access controls.

faq.question: Why is n8n taught alongside programmatic Python, and what will I build with it?
faq.answer: Module 07 (24 guided hours) covers enterprise business automation with self-hosted n8n. While Python is essential for custom algorithms and backend APIs, n8n excels at rapid event-driven integrations with third-party business software. You learn self-hosted Docker deployment, webhook triggers, CRM synchronization (HubSpot, Supabase, Google Sheets), scheduled automations, error workflows, and embedding AI reasoning nodes into enterprise operations.

faq.question: How is AI-assisted coding incorporated into the development workflow?
faq.answer: From Module 01, you learn professional AI-assisted development workflows using VS Code with GitHub Copilot and Cursor. You learn effective in-editor prompting, generating boilerplate code, drafting unit tests, explaining complex codebases, and diff-driven code reviews. Importantly, we emphasize verification hygiene: students must understand, trace, and validate every line of AI-generated code before committing.

faq.question: Which database systems and cloud deployment tools are taught?
faq.answer: You master PostgreSQL 16+ as your primary relational and vector data store, utilizing SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM and Alembic migrations. For deployment, Module 12 covers Docker containerization, multi-stage Dockerfiles, Docker Compose for multi-container orchestration, and deployment to cloud platforms (such as Render, Railway, or VPS environments) with environment variable security, reverse proxies, and healthcheck endpoints.

faq.question: How are AI systems evaluated, benchmarked, and secured against vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: Module 11 (24 guided hours) covers LLMOps evaluation and defensive security. You build golden test datasets, evaluate retrieval precision and generation faithfulness using automated rubrics, and implement distributed tracing with Langfuse or LangSmith. For security, you implement defenses against OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and Agentic Applications (2026), including prompt injection mitigation, indirect retrieval sanitization, least-privilege tool execution, and PII redaction.

faq.question: Why is the program 9 months (36 weeks) long, and how is the schedule structured?
faq.answer: True engineering competence requires structured progressive growth. 9 months (36 calendar weeks) allows students to move methodically from zero-coding foundations (Python, APIs, databases) through intermediate automations (n8n, LLM APIs) to advanced production architectures (RAG, LangGraph, MCP, Docker) and a comprehensive 4-stage capstone defense, ensuring knowledge is internalized through repetitive hands-on practice.

faq.question: What does the 360 guided instructional hours format include?
faq.answer: The 360 guided hours represent live, instructor-led training and interactive lab workshops delivered at a sustainable pace of 10 guided hours per week across 36 weeks. Sessions combine technical conceptual breakdowns, live code architecture demonstrations, interactive pair debugging, and guided hands-on implementation of lab exercises across all 14 curriculum modules.

faq.question: How much independent practice is required outside of class hours?
faq.answer: In addition to the 10 weekly guided hours, students are expected to invest 120–180 recommended independent practice hours across the 9 months (approximately 4–5 hours per week). This independent time is dedicated to completing lab exercises, writing automated test suites, building personal GitHub portfolio repositories, and preparing the final capstone project.

faq.question: What are the seven major portfolio builds created during the program?
faq.answer: You build 7 canonical, production-grade systems: (1) AI Research & Structured Reporting System, (2) Production AI API Microservice with FastAPI and Docker, (3) AI Lead Qualification & CRM Automation with n8n, (4) Enterprise RAG Knowledge Assistant with pgvector and reranking, (5) AI Customer Support & MCP Tool Agent, (6) Multi-Agent Research & Business Analytics System with LangGraph, and (7) Full-Stack Enterprise AI Operations System [Final Capstone].

faq.question: Will I need to pay for expensive software subscriptions or AI model API usage?
faq.answer: Nova Skills maintains a strict low-cost student tooling policy. We utilize open-source and free-tier tools wherever possible (VS Code, PostgreSQL, local Docker, open-source embeddings, and free community tiers of n8n and Supabase). For commercial frontier model APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic), guidance and optimizations are provided to keep total 9-month student consumption within an estimated ₹1,500–₹2,500 total, often covered via standard platform free-trial credits.

faq.question: Are there high cloud infrastructure or GPU hosting costs during the program?
faq.answer: No. All models are accessed through serverless inference APIs or lightweight local open-source models, eliminating any requirement for expensive dedicated GPU hardware. For hosting backend microservices and databases, students are guided through free and low-cost container hosting tiers (such as Render, Railway, or local Docker environments) that require zero ongoing cloud expenses during training.

faq.question: What is the total tuition fee for the 9-month AI Mastery program?
faq.answer: The base tuition fee is INR 89,900 before applicable statutory taxes. This includes the complete 360 guided instructional hours across 14 modules, mentorship, code reviews, access to all 7 portfolio project specifications, lab environments, capstone evaluation, and verified credential issuance.

faq.question: What is the applicable tax on the tuition fee, and is a GST invoice provided?
faq.answer: In accordance with statutory Indian tax regulations, an 18% Goods and Services Tax (GST) of INR 16,182 applies to the INR 89,900 base tuition, bringing the total payable amount to INR 106,082. A valid GST invoice with input tax credit eligibility is provided for all corporate-sponsored or business enrollments.

faq.question: Are installment and No-Cost EMI payment plans available?
faq.answer: Yes. Approved No-Cost EMI plans are available through authorized banking and financing partners for tenures up to 9 months, amounting to approximately INR 11,787 per month with zero interest penalty. Modular stage-based installment payment options are also available upon institutional approval.

faq.question: How are students mentored and assessed throughout the course?
faq.answer: Assessment is continuous and rigorous, evaluated against a standardized 100-point rubric: Engineering Implementation (30%), Reliability & Automated Testing (20%), Architecture & System Integration (15%), Security & Data Privacy (15%), Project Documentation (10%), and Independent Practical Defense (10%). Students receive weekly code reviews, milestone evaluations, and participate in a live oral viva voce capstone defense.

faq.question: What career and placement assistance does Nova Skills provide?
faq.answer: Students who successfully complete all 14 modules and pass the capstone defense receive comprehensive career support. This includes technical resume and GitHub portfolio optimization, architecture walkthrough rehearsals, technical mock interviews, and verified introductions to hiring partners through Nova Skills' employer network. In compliance with consumer protection guidelines, Nova Skills emphasizes merit-based proof of work and does not make dishonest unconditional job or salary guarantees.

faq.question: How does the course ensure my skills remain relevant as AI tools evolve rapidly?
faq.answer: The program focuses on enduring software engineering and architectural primitives rather than fleeting UI tools. By mastering Python, REST APIs, SQL, relational/vector databases, state machine graphs, structured JSON schemas, and open protocols like MCP, you build an architectural foundation that allows you to adapt to new frontier models, libraries, or SDK releases in hours rather than months.

Cross-encoder reranking (Cohere Rerank), grounded prompt context assembly, and automated inline source citation guardrails

lessons.lesson_title: Enterprise Document Ingestion, Parsing & Advanced Chunking
lessons.what_is_taught: RAG architecture vs fine-tuning trade-offs, business knowledge-base design, document extraction from PDFs, DOCX, and web text, text cleaning, normalization, chunking strategies (fixed-size, recursive, semantic, hierarchical), chunk overlap, and rich metadata tagging.
subtopics: RAG vs fine-tuning: when to retrieve dynamic knowledge vs when to adapt model weights
Enterprise knowledge-base design: structuring unstructured business repositories for retrieval
Document extraction pipelines: parsing complex PDFs, markdown, HTML, and tables with OCR fallback
Data cleaning and normalization: removing boilerplate, headers/footers, and sanitizing prompt injection vectors
Chunking strategies: comparing fixed-size, recursive character splitting, semantic chunking, and document hierarchy
Chunk overlap economics and metadata enrichment (document ID, section title, page numbers, tenant ID, permissions)

lessons.what_learner_does: Ingest a messy 100-page enterprise policy handbook, compare 3 chunking algorithms, enrich chunks with granular metadata, and evaluate chunk coherence.
lessons.expected_outcome: Production Document Parsing & Chunking Pipeline with Metadata Enrichment.

lessons.lesson_title: Embeddings, Vector Spaces & PostgreSQL pgvector Storage

subtopics: Mathematical vector representations: how text maps to high-dimensional embedding spaces
Evaluating embedding models: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small/large, voyage-3, and open-source models
PostgreSQL pgvector architecture: vector columns, indexing with HNSW and IVFFlat, tuning m and ef_construction
Similarity search queries: computing cosine distance (<=>) and inner product (<#>) in SQL
Metadata filtering: combining relational WHERE clauses with high-speed vector similarity
Multi-tenant knowledge isolation and role-based retrieval permissions at the database level
lessons.why_it_matters: Vector databases allow semantic similarity retrieval; native PostgreSQL pgvector eliminates external vector database silos while guaranteeing ACID transactions and enterprise permissions.
lessons.what_learner_does: Deploy PostgreSQL with pgvector on Supabase, create indexed vector tables, insert embedded document chunks, and execute permission-filtered similarity queries.
lessons.expected_outcome: High-Performance PostgreSQL pgvector Database with HNSW Indexing.

lessons.lesson_title: Hybrid Search, Reranking & Verifiable Source Citations
lessons.what_is_taught: Combining keyword full-text search (BM25) with dense vector search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), cross-encoder reranking (Cohere Rerank), query rewriting, prompt context assembly, and strict inline source citation guardrails.
subtopics: Limitations of pure vector search: failure with exact part numbers, acronyms, and legal identifiers
Hybrid search architecture: fusing PostgreSQL full-text search (tsvector/BM25) with vector similarity via RRF
Cross-encoder reranking: re-scoring top-50 candidates with Cohere Rerank to maximize top-5 precision
Query rewriting and expansion: generating sub-queries and hypothetical document embeddings (HyDE)
Context assembly: structuring the prompt envelope with strict grounding instructions and anti-hallucination rules
Verifiable source citations: enforcing inline citations [Doc, p. X] and building automated citation validation logic
lessons.why_it_matters: Enterprises cannot tolerate unverified assertions; hybrid search and cross-encoder reranking ensure pinpoint retrieval accuracy with verifiable citations.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build a hybrid retrieval pipeline that queries both keyword and vector indexes, reranks candidates, and injects context into a model with strict source attribution.
lessons.expected_outcome: Hybrid Retrieval & Reranking Engine with Verified Inline Citations.

RAG evaluation methodology: building golden question-answer test sets and measuring precision/recall
Automated evaluation metrics: measuring Faithfulness (hallucination detection) and Answer Relevance
Defending against indirect prompt injection embedded inside uploaded enterprise PDFs and docs
Latency and token cost optimization: caching embeddings, prompt compression, and batch queries
Major Portfolio Project 2 execution: deploying an authenticated enterprise knowledge assistant on FastAPI
lessons.why_it_matters: A static RAG pipeline rots as enterprise documents change; continuous indexing, automated evaluation, and security guardrails ensure lifelong production reliability.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build, evaluate, and package Major Portfolio Project 2: an authenticated enterprise knowledge assistant that answers complex queries, respects role permissions, and achieves >90% faithfulness on a golden test set.
lessons.expected_outcome: Authenticated Enterprise RAG Assistant with FastAPI backend, Supabase pgvector, and automated evaluation suite.

The ReAct cognitive loop: Thought, Action, Observation, and Final Answer mechanics
Single-agent architecture: system instructions, tool binding, and dynamic tool selection
Idempotent tool actions: preventing repeated billing, database corruption, or double-sending
Execution safeguards: max step limits, runaway loop detection, token budgets, and hard timeouts
Architectural discipline: why 80% of business tasks are best solved by a single focused agent with tools

lessons.lesson_title: LangGraph Foundations, State Machines & Durable Persistence

Defining strongly typed State schemas using TypedDict and Annotated reducers (add_messages)
Conditional routing: writing router functions that inspect agent state and branch execution dynamically
Durable execution and session persistence: saving agent state across requests with PostgresSaver
Handling failures and state recovery: resuming interrupted agent runs and replaying from checkpoints
Context management: trimming message histories, summarizing past conversation turns, and controlling token bloat
lessons.why_it_matters: Standard Python scripts lose memory on restart; LangGraph state machines persist agent state to PostgreSQL, allowing resilient multi-turn interactions that survive crashes.
lessons.what_learner_does: Construct a LangGraph state machine that manages a customer inquiry, persists state to PostgreSQL, and restores session history seamlessly across disconnected client calls.
lessons.expected_outcome: Durable LangGraph State Machine with PostgreSQL Checkpointing.

lessons.lesson_title: Human-in-the-Loop Approval Gates & Guardrails
lessons.what_is_taught: Implementing pause-and-resume human checkpoints (interrupt_before, interrupt_after), state editing, user approval workflows, action guardrails, and graceful escalation to human operators.

State inspection and modification: allowing human supervisors to inspect, edit, or reject agent actions before resumption

Agent guardrails: restricting tool execution based on user authentication roles and spending thresholds
Escalation protocols: transferring frustrated or high-risk customer sessions directly to human support staff

lessons.what_learner_does: Implement a human approval checkpoint in the support agent that automatically pauses when a refund exceeds ₹2,000, requesting human sign-off before executing.

Designing dual-transport MCP servers capable of running locally or deployed as cloud microservices

Rate limiting, request throttling, structured server audit logging, and compliance tracking

lessons.lesson_title: Enterprise Technical Discovery & Process Mapping
lessons.what_is_taught: Conducting technical discovery interviews with non-technical business stakeholders, gathering requirements, mapping complex manual business workflows using Mermaid/Miro flowcharts, identifying operational bottlenecks, and evaluating data availability and quality.

Requirements elicitation: uncovering hidden operational steps, exception paths, and legacy constraints
Visual process mapping: creating current-state vs future-state workflow diagrams using Mermaid syntax

Classifying process complexity: identifying deterministic business logic vs probabilistic cognitive tasks
Synthesizing technical discovery findings into a concise Business Requirements Document (BRD)

lessons.what_learner_does: Conduct a simulated discovery interview for an enterprise client, map the current manual workflow in Mermaid, and author a structured discovery brief.

Technical risk and compliance review: identifying regulatory, data privacy, and intellectual property constraints
Proof-of-Concept (PoC) planning: scoping a 2-week validation prototype with clear success thresholds

lessons.what_learner_does: Evaluate 3 competing business problems using the Feasibility Matrix, select the appropriate architecture, and draft a technical risk mitigation plan.
